reason: This is the only offered action, and it may start the chemical weathering needed to carry dissolved material into the sea.

reaction: The qualification that it does not instantly dissolve rock is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly advances weathering.
expectation: The acidic rain will react with minerals in the basalt, releasing some dissolved material.

reason: Runoff toward the basin seems the most direct way to carry dissolved material toward the sea.

reason: Combining the runoff with the sea directly advances the dissolved-material goal.

reaction: The reminder that early seawater need not resemble modern seawater is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may advance the remaining sediment goal.

reaction: The distinction between transported particles and dissolved material is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should move the particles toward the basin.
expectation: Runoff will carry the fine particles toward the sea, where they may later settle.

reaction: The contrast between cloudy sediment and invisible dissolved material is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the remaining sediment goal.

reaction: It was satisfying to see the solid sediment pathway end in a visible bed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Loosening particles from altered basalt made the distinction between solid sediment and dissolved ions clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive runoff transport steps felt somewhat repetitive, even though they showed the two pathways.

surprise.text: Clear-looking runoff can carry rock-derived ions, while suspended particles form a separate, visible load.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though most choices were the only offered combination, so I was following the menu rather than discovering compatibility.

continue.text: Yes. The concise explanations of weathering and transport made me curious to see another natural process, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
